name: sf90-hammer-point
note: Single-point wreck citation (157k) plus outlier-wide clean range. hand-converted 2026-08-17 from the recorded freeform findings into typed comps, each as its source stated it.

areas.description: Entire front fascia, lower bumper, and splitter torn off and missing; headlight housings displaced. Panels behind (hood, fenders) appear to retain their shape, so damage looks concentrated in bolt-on fascia/bumper components rather than structure, but impact force needed to remove them this cleanly raises suspicion of hidden radiator support or rail contact.

Left front wheel and tire completely missing, exposing brake caliper, hub, and control arm; wheel well liner and lower fascia torn away. Consistent with a hard corner impact that could have bent suspension or knuckle even if rail itself is not visibly torn.

Rear bumper cover and diffuser shroud removed/hanging, exposing hybrid inverter wiring, exhaust tips, and rear crash beam; taillights and engine cover glass intact, no visible tearing of rear rails or subframe in these photos.
Small chip/crack visible at lower corner of windshield; otherwise glass intact.

With front and rear fascias off, hybrid high-voltage cabling, inverter box, and exhaust/diffuser hardware are exposed to the elements and yard handling; unknown whether wiring or coolant lines were compromised in the impact versus during disassembly for parts.

Missing left front wheel entirely and exposed hub/caliper strongly suggest a hard direct impact to that corner; right side wheels appear seated normally in rear 3/4 shots but front-left geometry cannot be assessed with the wheel gone.
Cabin looks clean and undamaged, seats, dash, and steering wheel airbag cover intact with no deployment evidence; low mileage (3004 mi) shown on cluster.

observations.note: Front clip torn away, left front wheel/tire missing entirely exposing brake caliper and hub, front bumper and fascia shredded, hood edge crumpled.
Left side profile confirms front fascia and left front corner completely torn off; rear bumper cover also missing exposing hybrid wiring harness and rear crash structure.
Rear 3/4 view shows rear bumper fascia removed, diffuser/exhaust exposed, right side fender scuffed but shape intact; wheels look square (no obvious camber loss visible from this angle).
Front right corner view shows fascia hanging, headlight area disturbed, radiator support/core visible but rails behind it not clearly deformed.
Straight-on front view shows lower fascia torn away, small crack/chip on windshield lower corner, hood shut line normal suggesting hood and frame above headlights not grossly bent.
Rear straight-on view: bumper cover off, taillights intact, exhaust/diffuser assembly hanging loose but rear crash beam appears present, no visible tearing of the tub or rear subframe rails.
Interior right seat area clean, no airbag deployment, no fire/water staining.
Interior dash/steering wheel view - dash intact, no airbag deployment visible, steering wheel airbag cover intact.
Instrument cluster shows only 3004 miles, warning lights for system-not-programmed (likely from battery disconnect) and low-voltage/hybrid faults, but no crash-related SRS deployment message legible.
Rear engine cover/hatch view shows glass intact, rear grille panel present, no fire or heat discoloration visible.
Hood/cowl close-up shows panel gaps uniform, no buckling, confirming hood itself is not majorly deformed despite lower fascia loss.
VIN/data plate photo, no damage information, confirms car identity ZFF96NLA2M0263155.

triage.drivetrainRisk: No engine or transmission components are visibly missing or damaged in these photos, and the rear clamshell/engine cover glass looks intact, but with the front fascia gone and the left front wheel completely detached, a hard front-corner impact is likely — this can transmit shock into the front-mounted hybrid motor/inverter and cooling radiators even without visible rail damage; the exposed hybrid wiring at the rear also needs high-voltage isolation testing before any diagnostics or work begins.
